sectors.trend: Mixed: coal booms domestically (72) and Premier pushes coal consolidation (23), but gold/silver prices slip on geopolitical risk (3,7). Multiple WA/Qld gold discoveries (43,64,65,38,39) and lithium exploration (40) support junior miners. Mineral Resources clears ASIC overhang (67).
sectors.implications: Coal names (WBC.AX, BHP.AX coal division) benefit from domestic demand and policy support. Gold juniors (Gateway, King River, Moonlight, PLC) see positive exploration catalysts despite spot price weakness. BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face headwind from oil-driven inflation fears pressuring global growth.

sectors.trend: Under pressure from rate hike fears (58), mortgage stress at 18-year highs (47), and housing downturn risk (59). CBA faces reputational hit over 13-year inactive card fees (54). Property developer collapses (51,76) raise NPL concerns.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin pressure from rate cycle but benefit from higher yields. Housing credit risk and developer defaults (Bathla, mega developer) threaten loan books. Bond yield spike (10,62) supports net interest margins short-term.

sectors.trend: Oil spike from US-Iran war (16,62) lifts energy sentiment. Chinese solar overtakes coal globally (44) but Australian coal booms domestically (72). Chevron-Microsoft 20-year AI power deal (4) signals structural energy demand.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WDS.AX, SXG.AX benefit from oil price strength. Coal producers gain from domestic policy support. Long-term energy transition (solar) is a structural theme but near-term oil volatility dominates.

sectors.trend: Qantas ground crews vote to strike (75) threatens QAN.AX operations. Inflation 'home grown' (71) and per capita recession (66) pressure consumer spending. Grocery theft rising (37) signals household stress.
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces operational risk from industrial action. WES.AX, WOW.AX, CPL.AX face margin pressure from input costs. Defensive consumer staples relatively resilient.

sectors.trend: AI bubble warnings from BoE (2), Iran conflict disrupts tech (50), but Citi recommends buying tumbling tech (55). Microsoft-Chevron power deal (4) and Nvidia 70% revenue jump (2) show structural AI demand intact.
sectors.implications: Limited direct ASX exposure but CSL.AX (biotech/health tech) and Canva (60) face sentiment spillover. AI disruption to jobs (8,70) is a medium-term structural theme.

sectors.trend: Housing 'bloodbath' forecast (59), 10% price drop risk (58), mega developer collapse (51), Bathla near insolvency (76). Mortgage stress at 18-year highs (47).
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX, DGL.AX) face occupancy and valuation pressure. Residential property developers at high risk. Commercial REITs relatively insulated but rate-sensitive.

key_themes: Geopolitical risk (US-Iran war) driving oil spike and global risk-off
RBA fourth rate hike looming amid home-grown inflation (71)
Housing market correction risk with 10% downside and developer defaults
Productivity deterioration and per capita recession despite headline GDP
Coal sector policy support vs global energy transition
AI bubble debate: structural demand vs valuation risk

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA rate hike / bond yield spike
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce duration exposure; favour short-duration and floating-rate instruments; overweight rate-sensitive banks for NIM benefit
Underweight residential REITs and property developers; monitor bank NPL provisions; favour commercial/industrial REITs
Hedge with energy exposure (WES.AX, WDS.AX); maintain cash buffer; monitor AUD/USD for risk-off flows
Favour defensive sectors (healthcare, consumer staples); avoid cyclical consumer names
Reduce QAN.AX exposure pending resolution; monitor Qantas earnings guidance
Diversify away from concentrated AI/tech positions; favour cash-generative tech over speculative

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight coal and energy names on domestic policy support and oil spike
opportunities.rationale: Coal boom (72), Premier's consolidation push (23), and oil-driven inflation support WES.AX, WBC.AX energy segment, WDS.AX

opportunities.rationale: Fourth rate hike (58) and bond yield spike (10,62) support net interest margins; CBA.AX fee issue (54) is isolated

opportunities.recommendation: Lithium and critical minerals exploration plays

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce residential REIT and property developer exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: 10% house price downside (58), developer collapses (51,76), 18-year mortgage stress (47) create tail risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Trim Qantas and cyclical consumer exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Strike vote (75) and per capita recession (66) pressure QAN.AX and consumer discretionary

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain cash/short-duration bond allocation as hedge
defensive_moves.rationale: Geopolitical uncertainty (16,50), rate volatility (62,10), and inflation uncertainty (71) favour liquidity
Per capita recession (66) and productivity decline (45) favour defensive income; CSL.AX, WES.AX staples resilient

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure over 1-3 months. Fourth RBA rate hike, oil-driven inflation, and housing correction fears dominate. Bond yield volatility (10,62) creates two-way risk. Geopolitical escalation (US-Iran) adds tail risk. Expect ^AXJO to trade in a range with downside bias unless oil stabilises.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive if inflation peaks and RBA pivots. Productivity concerns (45,73) and per capita recession (66) cap upside. Coal-to-solar transition (44) and mining exploration pipeline (36,38,39,40,43,64,65,68) provide structural support for materials. Housing correction (58,59) may create value in commercial REITs and banks post-stabilisation.
